answer: As a big cricket fan, I did not have to think very long about this one. A sportsperson I genuinely admire is a famous cricketer from my country, who is something of a national hero. He has played for Bangladesh for many years, and he has been part of some of the team's most memorable victories against much bigger cricketing nations. Beyond his obvious talent, what I admire is the [[humility]] he shows despite enormous fame. He came from a modest background and worked his way up through sheer [[perseverance]], which makes his story relatable to ordinary people. On the field he is famous for staying calm under pressure, a quality that separates good players from truly great ones. What impresses me most is his [[consistency]]; he performs at a high level year after year, which requires incredible discipline. Off the field, he is known for his charity work, which shows real character. I think athletes like him are role models precisely because of how they carry themselves, not just their statistics. His [[dignity]] in both victory and defeat is something young people can genuinely learn from. I still remember watching one of his match-winning innings with my father and younger sister, all of us shouting at the television and my mother rushing in from the kitchen to see what had happened. Honestly, he makes the whole nation proud, and rightly so, and whenever he walks out to bat, the entire country seems to hold its breath.

followUps.q: Have you ever watched him play live?
followUps.answer: Not yet, unfortunately. Tickets for big matches in Dhaka sell out quickly, and it is a long journey from Sirajganj. But watching him in a stadium is definitely on my [[bucket list]].
Only casually these days. I played a lot as a child with friends in the neighbourhood, but now I mostly watch it, usually with my father, who is an even bigger fan than I am.
